memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Marcus identified two viable nonstop economy itineraries for the April 13-14 Atlanta meeting. Both use the earlier Monday departure from O'Hare; the Tuesday return remains open pending the venue and final meeting end time.

messages.content: I need a round trip from Chicago to Atlanta for a regional leadership meeting Monday, April 13 through Tuesday, April 14. The opening session is at 2:00 Monday, and I should be able to leave after 5:30 Tuesday. The venue hasn't been finalized yet.
Understood. Will you be traveling from O'Hare, Midway, or either airport? Also, should I limit this to nonstop economy flights?
Either airport is possible, but O'Hare is easier. Nonstop economy only. I need enough time after landing to get across Atlanta without cutting it close.

For Monday, two practical outbound windows stand out. Candidate A leaves ORD around 7:10 a.m. and reaches ATL around 10:15 a.m., leaving roughly three hours and forty-five minutes before the session. Candidate B leaves ORD around 8:45 a.m. and arrives around 11:50 a.m., which is workable but gives you about two hours and ten minutes before the start. I would avoid arrivals after noon until the venue is known.
Agreed. What can I do Tuesday evening? The meeting may finish at 5:30, but that could shift to 6:00 once they publish the agenda.

There are two sensible return windows. Candidate A departs ATL around 7:45 p.m. and arrives at ORD around 9:05 p.m. Candidate B leaves around 9:05 p.m. and reaches ORD around 10:25 p.m. The earlier one works if you are released at 5:30 and the venue is reasonably close to the airport; the later one is safer if the meeting runs until 6:00 or is held north of downtown.
Put together two complete combinations. I don't need the absolute cheapest if it creates a tight transfer to or from the meeting.

Best schedule: ORD 7:10 a.m. to ATL 10:15 a.m. Monday, then ATL 7:45 p.m. to ORD 9:05 p.m. Tuesday. It protects the arrival and still gets you home at a reasonable hour. More cautious return: use the same 7:10 a.m. outbound and take the 9:05 p.m. return, arriving around 10:25 p.m. That adds substantial post-meeting margin. The 8:45 a.m. outbound is a fallback, not one of my top two combinations, because Atlanta traffic could consume most of its cushion.
Keep both of those. Don't book anything yet. Once I have the venue and firm Tuesday cutoff, we'll choose the return and look for a hotel nearby.

I’ll carry forward the 7:10 a.m. ORD departure with two Tuesday returns: 7:45 p.m. as the earlier option and 9:05 p.m. for more schedule protection. Nothing is booked. The next step is to confirm the Atlanta venue and whether the meeting ends at 5:30 or 6:00, then compare nearby hotels and finalize the flight pairing.

updated_continuity_summary: Marcus is planning an April 13-14 round trip from Chicago to Atlanta for a regional leadership meeting. He retained an early Monday ORD-ATL flight and two Tuesday ATL-ORD return options, one around 7:45 p.m. and another around 9:05 p.m. Nothing is booked. The Atlanta venue and whether Tuesday's meeting ends at 5:30 or 6:00 remain unresolved; once confirmed, he plans to choose the return and search for a nearby hotel.
